items.title: Library supplement: Weighted gradient integration by parts on product spheres

source.attribution: Generic exposition of classical sphere calculus; no primary-textbook completion or novelty claim.

items.statement: For arbitrary \(n,N\in\mathbb N\), use \(E=\mathbb R^{n+1}\), its unit sphere \(S\), \(M=S^{\operatorname{Fin}N}\), the induced product smooth and metric structures, and the exact normalized polar product measure \(\mu=\sigma^{\otimes N}\) defined below. For every real \(f,\rho\in C^1(M)\) and \(g\in C^2(M)\), define the actual tangent field \(V_i=\rho\nabla_i g\). Then the three displayed integrands are integrable, its divergence has zero integral, and the weighted integration-by-parts identity holds. The field regularity and tangency are derived from these hypotheses. The weight \(\rho\) has no sign or normalization restriction.
assumptions: \(n,N\in\mathbb N\) are arbitrary, with no positivity restriction. Thus the ambient dimension is \(n+1\); \(n=0\) gives the two-point sphere and \(N=0\) gives a one-point empty product.

The scalar field is \(\mathbb R\). All norms, inner products, tangent projections and manifold metrics are induced by the Euclidean structure. Regularity means regularity in the usual stereographic sphere charts and their finite product charts.

The reference measure is exactly \(\mu=\sigma^{\otimes N}\), with \(\sigma=\tau(S)^{-1}\tau\) and \(\tau=\operatorname{vol}_E.\mathrm{toSphere}\). Its finite nonzero mass and probability normalization are proved internally; they are not extra inputs.
For every \(f,\rho,g:M\to\mathbb R\), assume \(f,\rho\in C^1(M)\) and \(g\in C^2(M)\), jointly in all configuration coordinates.

The field is defined by \(V_i(x)=\rho(x)\nabla_i g(x)\). Its C¹ regularity and pointwise tangency are derived. No sign, strict positivity, normalization, or density interpretation is assumed for \(\rho\).

bindings.boundary: This is a static integration identity for the specified normalized polar measure and its finite product. It gives no derivative in time, entropy evolution, diffusion existence, or density PDE. Identifying another supplied measure, gradient, divergence, or model generator with these definitions is a separate application obligation. The proof derives the required radial regularity from the intrinsic hypotheses. It neither assumes nor asserts that the totalized radial extension is continuous or differentiable at the origin. All integrals are ordinary finite real integrals. The conclusions include integrability, and no almost-everywhere-in-time or finite-horizon convention is involved. The zero-dimensional sphere and empty product are included. The proof retains the radial factor \(r^n/r\) on positive radii; it does not replace the exponent by truncated natural subtraction. The stated regularity is classical C¹/C². No weak-gradient, Sobolev, nonsmooth-weight, or arbitrary-measure extension is claimed. If \(\rho\) is later called a probability density, its nonnegativity and normalization must be supplied by that application. The present geometric identity does not assert them.
